summary: In Nazareth, Gabriel tells the virgin Mary she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear Jesus, the Son of God, heir to David’s throne. Mary believes.
key_insight: Zacharias asked, “How shall I know this?” and was struck silent. Mary asked, “How can this be?” and was given an answer. The words sound alike, but Zacharias wanted proof, while Mary believed and asked how God would do it; Elizabeth will soon call her “she who believed” (Luke 1:45).
story: In the sixth month of Elizabeth’s pregnancy, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a town in Galilee. He came to a virgin named Mary, who was betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David.
The angel came in and said, “Rejoice, highly favored one, the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women!” Mary was troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this could be.

“Do not be afraid, Mary,” he said, “for you have found favor with God.” She would conceive and bear a Son and call His name JESUS. “He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Highest; and the Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David. And He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of His kingdom there will be no end.”

Mary asked, “How can this be, since I do not know a man?” The angel answered, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Highest will overshadow you; therefore, also, that Holy One who is to be born will be called the Son of God.”
Then he told her that her relative Elizabeth, who had been called barren, had conceived a son in her old age and was now in her sixth month. “For with God nothing will be impossible.”
Mary said, “Behold the maidservant of the Lord! Let it be to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.

scene.label: Nazareth
scene.text: A small village in the hills of lower Galilee, never mentioned in the Old Testament or by the Jewish historian Josephus. Gabriel’s first announcement came to a priest in Jerusalem; this one passes by the capital and comes to a village of no reputation.

scene.label: Betrothed
scene.text: Betrothal was far more binding than engagement today. It was a legal commitment, usually lasting about a year before the wife moved into her husband’s home, and it could be ended only by divorce. Girls were often betrothed young, so Mary was probably in her teens.

scene.label: “Highly favored”
scene.text: The word means one to whom grace has been given. The angel explains it himself: “you have found favor with God.” The honor is God’s gift, and Mary answers it by calling herself the Lord’s servant.

scene.label: “Overshadow”
scene.text: The Greek Old Testament uses the same word for the cloud of God’s glory that rested on the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35), and Luke uses it again for the cloud at the Transfiguration (Luke 9:34). The conception would be the work of God’s own presence.

witnesses.luke: Only Luke tells of Gabriel’s visit to Mary. Matthew tells the birth from Joseph’s side; Luke tells it from Mary’s, including what only she could know, and twice notes that she kept these things in her heart (Luke 2:19, 51). He sets the young woman of Nazareth beside the aged priest in the temple, and it is the young woman who believes.

seeing.reveals: Jesus is both fully human and the Son of God: conceived in a woman’s womb, yet by the power of the Holy Spirit. He is the promised heir of David, and His kingdom will have no end.
seeing.living: Mary’s yes put her good name at risk; even Joseph at first planned to send her away (Matthew 1:19). Yet she called herself “the maidservant of the Lord” and placed herself at God’s disposal. Faith does not wait for every question to be answered before it says yes to God’s word.
seeing.ponder: Where is God asking you to say, as Mary did, “Let it be to me according to your word”?

preaching.big_idea: Nothing is impossible with God, and faith answers His word with, “Let it be to me.”
outline: A King whose kingdom will not end (30–33)
A holy Child by the Spirit’s power (34–37)
preaching.watch_for: Gabriel’s words in verses 32–33 echo God’s promise to David: a son, a throne, a house and a kingdom “forever” (2 Samuel 7:12–16). Verse 37 echoes God’s question to Abraham about Sarah: “Is anything too hard for the LORD?” (Genesis 18:14).
